Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:1: After we have explained in the previous chapters that there is fear from judgment and fear from death, we thought it fitting to resolve a difficulty that arises here from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who explains in Parashat Bereshit (Zohar 11b), and likewise in the Tikkunim, that fear of death and fear of Gehinnom is an external fear. In these words: "in the place where fear dwells, below there is an 'evil fear' that strikes and smites and accuses, and it is a strap to flog the wicked; and whoever fears because of the punishment of flogging and accusation, as stated, that fear of the LORD called 'the fear of the LORD unto life' does not rest upon him - rather, that evil fear rests upon him, and it is found that that strap, evil fear, and not the fear of the LORD, rests upon him" - to this point. And it explains further on that "evil fear" is the evil strap, the punishments of the wicked, the four death penalties of the court, which come from the side of the four husks: chaos, void, darkness, deep.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:2: And so too in the Tikkunim, at the start of Tikkun 33 (page 76b), it says: there is fear and there is fear. The fear of the LORD - this is the Shechinah, the holy Malchut; the evil fear - this is the strap to flog the wicked, and what is it? The poison of death of Samael, his female counterpart. The fear of the LORD is a reward for one who guards the negative commandments; the evil fear is a strap to flog one who transgresses them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:3: And further, in the Tikkunim (there, 5b), it says: there is fear and there is fear - not all faces are alike. There is a fear in which a person fears the Holy One, blessed be He, so that He not flog him with the strap, of which it is said (Genesis 1:2), "and the earth was chaos and void" - from the side of the Tree of Good and Evil, which is the empty land, the evil maidservant, similar to one of the four primary categories of damage, which is the Pit [Bor]; and similar to the pit of Joseph, of which it was established, "and the pit was empty," and so on - "the pit," the evil female; "pit" [bor], the male. And "bor" [also meaning "boor"], because from there it was established of him, "an ignoramus [bor] cannot be pious" - meaning, [he cannot be pious] because he lacks the fear of the LORD, which fears because of the Torah, which is Tiferet, from which it emerges - because it [the fear] is weighed against it [Tiferet]. And therefore not every fear is equal - for the fear of the LORD is His Malchut, which includes all the commandments of the Torah, because it is a fear that emerges from within the Torah, which is the central pillar, which is YHVH - for this reason the masters of the Mishnah established, "great is Torah, for it brings a person to deeds" - for if a person does not know the Torah, and the reward of its commandments, and its punishments for one who transgresses its commandments, and who created the Torah, and who gave it to Israel - how can he fear it and guard its commandments? And therefore David said to Solomon his son (I Chronicles 28:9), "know the God of your father and serve Him" - for if a person does not recognize the One who gave him the Torah and appointed him to guard it, how can he fear Him and perform His commandments? And therefore the Rabbis established, "an unlearned person cannot be pious, and an ignoramus cannot fear sin" - because the Torah, which is 611 [commandments], is given from two levels, from Chesed and Gevurah, from which come the two commandments: love, which is Chesed, and fear, which is Gevurah, which is Yirah, through which the 613 commandments are completed. And because the whole Torah and its commandments are given from two levels, the Rabbis established, "an ignoramus cannot fear sin, and an unlearned person cannot be pious" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:4: Behold, it is explicitly proven that the ignoramus [bor] fears the punishment and not the sin - and this raises a difficulty for us: why did Rashbi, peace be upon him, write all the punishments mentioned in the Heichalot of impurity and in other places?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:5: And it is possible to say that it is so that ignoramuses and those lacking understanding will hear of the punishments and turn back because of the punishment, and thereby, through [service] not for its own sake, come to fulfill fear for its own sake, as the good fear explained in this discourse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:6: And regarding our difficulty, that fear of death also appears to be a fear because of the externality, the evil strap that comes from the side of death, we may resolve it thus: the evil fear, condemned in this discourse, is when one fears to transgress a negative commandment of the Torah lest he be flogged; for "fear" simply put is the fear of [transgressing] a negative commandment, not to transgress what the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded him. And if he fears to transgress because of the strap, he is an ignoramus and condemned; but the essential thing is that he should fear to transgress out of fear of sin [itself] - as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the discourse, that there are several distinctions in the fear of sin; and therefore it says, "an ignoramus cannot fear sin," precisely - meaning the essential thing is that he fear not to transgress a negative commandment because of the sin [itself]. And what we find of fear because of death is a fear for the fulfillment of positive commandments, for he fears being lax in performing the commandments and repairing his soul, lest death overtake him first, and he be found going to his eternal home empty of good deeds. And of this the Sages commanded (Avot 4:16), "prepare yourself in the antechamber so that you may enter the banquet hall"; and likewise (ibid. 2:10), "repent one day before your death," and many similar statements. And so too in the discourse we copied above from Parashat Naso (127a), that King David, peace be upon him, said, "bless the LORD, O my soul," before you depart from the world, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:7: And also, if he hastens to fulfill a commandment because he fears that if he neglects it he will be punished - along the lines of what they said in the Gemara (Menachot 41a), that "at a time of divine wrath, they penalize [even the omission of] a positive commandment" - and likewise one who neglected the reading of the Shema, morning and evening, of whom it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:15), "that which is crooked cannot be made straight," and many similar cases - and he fears to neglect it because of the punishment, he is not for this reason called an ignoramus; for the essence of the ignoramus is that he directs his attention to the negative and positive commandments and does everything because of the punishment [alone], whereas the wise man fears not to transgress because of the sin [itself].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:8: And one must be precise, for behold, Rashbi, peace be upon him, mentioned in this discourse, within the general category of fear, the fear of punishments, as he wrote, "for if a person does not know the Torah, and the reward of its commandments, and its punishments for one who transgresses its commandments, how can he fear it," and so on; and if these are not needed for [proper] fear, why do we need to know them, and why were they written in the Zohar in several places?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:9: And it is possible to resolve this in three ways. The first: because once the sinner sees how great the punishment is for what he transgressed, according to the severity of the punishment he will seek to do his repentance accordingly - along the lines of "repentance according to the scale [of the sin]," as explained in the penances of Rabbi Elazar of Germiza [Rokeach].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:10: The second: we may say that although the wise man sees the punishments for matters, we need not conclude from this that his fear is of the punishment - rather, it is of the sin [itself]. This is that he fears the blemish that will come to darken his soul, so that it will need the refining of Gehinnom - along the lines of the "filthy garments" that would clothe the soul, as I explained above - and he will say in his heart: it is not fitting that I hand my soul, which is a portion of God from above, into the hand of the external one, the evil servant, to rule over it - for then I would be found blemishing the honor of my Maker, and it would be found (Proverbs 30:21), "under three things the earth trembles... under a servant when he becomes king," and so on. And along these lines we find that the Torah warned (Exodus 21:7), "and if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant, she shall not go out as the male slaves do"; and likewise, "he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people" (ibid. 21:8), as the Sava explains in Parashat Mishpatim (96a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:11: The third: we may say that the punishments were written because according to the level of the sin, so must the blemish of the soul be purified accordingly - and the proof is what Rashbi explained concerning the seven Heichalot of impurity, and likewise in the Midrash Ruth (Zohar Chadash 79a) concerning the seven compartments, that such-and-such a sin is recorded in such-and-such a Heichal and such-and-such a compartment. And the reason is that according to how far he descended and blemished his soul, so must it descend to the place of that particular compartment - and through this he comes to distance himself from the sin, because it defiles the soul to such-and-such a degree of impurity, such that to purify that impurity he must descend to such-and-such a place - and this remains, forever, fear because of the sin [itself].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:12: And the evil fear, which is fear because of the evil strap, is explained in this baraita, which is brought in the book Sefer HaRokeach, in the root of fear; in these words: in the Baraita of Rabbi Pinchas: there are those who serve the Holy One, blessed be He, in fear and dread, and in great dread and much terror, and they pray to be saved from the curses written concerning those who betray His commandments and those who transgress the ordinances of the Holy One, blessed be He, both in this world and in the World to Come. In this world - from illnesses and blows and pains, and that they not need [to depend on] other people, and that strangers not rule over them, and that they not see death or evil in their offspring, and that their days be filled with good and blessing. And in the World to Come - to be saved from retribution, from destruction, and from the burning fire of Gehinnom, destined to blaze and consume the wicked for the great Day of Judgment, for which a sin-offering is brought - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:13: And concerning the good fear, four things were mentioned: the first, "for if a person does not know the Torah," and so on; the second, "and who created the Torah"; the third, "and who gave it to Israel"; the fourth, "for if a person does not recognize the One who gave him the Torah and appointed him to guard it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:14: And of these four, the essential ones are three. The first: to fear the Cause of all causes and the Reason of all reasons, for He is the One who gave us the Torah, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, said in the discourse we copied in chapter 1 of this Gate - that the essence of fear is to fear the Holy One, blessed be He, because He is the root and source of all worlds; and thus one who demeans [the Torah] by not performing a commandment, or transgresses a negative commandment, touches the honor of his Maker, and is found, Heaven forfend, demeaning the Master of all, the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, who commanded him to do it. And this is what is meant by "and who created the Torah."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:15: The second: fear because of the blemish that will reach the Torah - and this is what was precisely stated, "for if a person does not recognize the One who gave him the Torah and appointed him to guard it." And the matter is that the whole Torah depends on the emanation of the supernal attributes, as we shall elaborate, with God's help, on the greatness of the Torah; and it is known that the attributes cleave to the Emanator, He and His attributes being one within them - and this exact correspondence applies to the Torah as well: He and His Torah are one. And just as a blemish reaches the attributes through the cause of sin, as explained in the previous chapters, so that they are blemished and lose their cleaving to the Emanator, and the light is withheld from them - correspondingly, a blemish reaches the Torah; and just as a blemish reaches the soul of Atzilut, as explained in chapter 9, so it reaches the Torah of Atzilut, for there is a Torah of Atzilut and a Torah of Beriah, as explained in the Tikkunim (4b). And corresponding to this distinction, it first says, "for if a person does not know the Torah" - meaning, the essential nature of the Torah itself, for from this comes great reward for one who fulfills its commandments, or punishment for one who neglects them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:16: The third: "and who gave it to Israel." And the matter is that it is known that the souls of Israel are refined from the seventy nations, for "Jacob, the LORD's own portion [chose Him] as His treasure" (cf. Psalms 135:4), and likewise (Deuteronomy 32:9), "for the LORD's portion is His people, Jacob is the lot of His inheritance," and likewise it says (ibid. 10:15), "only in your fathers did the LORD delight, to love them, and He chose their seed after them, you, above all peoples," and so on. And since the Holy One, blessed be He, out of His abundant love, chose the fathers and made them the root for all the holy souls, and our souls are children to them, nursing from the root of the fathers - therefore the son must resemble his father; and therefore it says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Rabbah, chapter 25) that a person is obligated to say, "when will my deeds reach the deeds of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?" and so on - and we will copy his full words, with God's help, in the coming Gate, in the commentary.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:17: Besides this, "Jacob is the lot [chevel] of His inheritance" - meaning that the six hundred thousand souls of Israel are all bound one to another like this rope [chevel], woven as one unit without separation; and just as a taut rope, if you shake one end, the whole shakes - so too, if one man sins, He is wrathful at the whole congregation, as in the incident of Achan (Joshua 7), the reason being that all Israel are guarantors for one another. My teacher, peace be upon him, elaborated on the reason for this in the book Pardes, Gate of Intention, chapter 1; and therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Yevamot 64a) that the Shechinah does not rest upon Israel when they number fewer than six hundred thousand - and it says, behold, were there six hundred thousand less one, and each and every one withheld himself from procreation, he causes the Shechinah to depart from Israel. And as Rashbi explains (Bereshit 2b), "from the greatness of His might and the strength of His power, not one is missing" (Isaiah 40:26) - that every time Israel was counted, even though there was a plague or the like among them, they never fell short of six hundred thousand - to teach that the whole six hundred thousand are one unity. It follows that one who blemishes [his soul] blemishes all the souls of Israel, until he returns to fix what he damaged from the side of his own soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:18: And further, [Israel] are "the portion of YHVH," as it says (Deuteronomy 32:9), "for the portion of YHVH is His people" - and the intent is that the portions, once they have this relation to one another, do not separate; and it says that a portion from the name YHVH is below with His people, who are Israel - and this is along the lines of (Joshua 7:9), "and they shall cut off our name from the earth, and what will You do for Your great Name?" - for a portion of His Name is held together with us. And it also says that a portion of our souls is held above with His Name - and this is "for the portion of YHVH" - in that portion of YHVH, His people are held and rooted with His Name. And it is found from this that one who blemishes his soul, since it is bound to YHVH, brings, Heaven forfend, a blemish to YHVH - and this premise is necessarily so of itself, as we explained above in chapter 9.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:19: Further, it is explained in the Tikkunim (Zohar Chadash 110a) that from the three yuds in the [spelled-out] Name - yud vav dalet, dalet vav yud, vav yud vav [spellings of the letters of the Tetragrammaton] - the nefesh, ruach, and neshamah of Israel are drawn; and of this it is said (Deuteronomy 14:2), "and the LORD has chosen you to be His own treasured people" - "His own treasure, YYY [an acronym alluding to the three yuds]." And all this may be said in explaining "and who gave it to Israel" - for since Israel possesses these virtues, one who blemishes his soul, which is part of the community of Israel, blemishes all that has been said.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:20: And I have seen fit, to complete this Gate, to explain the important fear that a person should choose. Concerning the virtue of fear, it says in the Mechilta, Parashat Shemini, in these words, on the verse (Leviticus 9:6), "and Moses said, this is the thing which the LORD commanded that you shall do": Moses said to Israel, remove that evil inclination from your hearts, and be all of you in one fear and one counsel, to serve before the Omnipresent; just as He is unique in the world, so shall your service be unified before Him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:16), "and you shall circumcise the foreskin of your hearts," and so on. For what reason? "For the LORD your God, He is God of gods," and so on. And if you do so - "and the glory of the LORD shall appear to you" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:21: "Moses said to Israel," and so on - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, were compelled to this interpretation of the verse because this verse is superfluous and has no [independent] meaning otherwise: for above, Scripture says (Leviticus 9:2), "and he said to Aaron, take for yourself," and so on, and afterward (ibid. 9:3), "and to the children of Israel you shall speak, saying, take a goat," and so on - if so, what is "and Moses said"? Was it not already stated through Aaron? And if he wished to say something else, he would say, "this thing you shall do" - and what is it? It does not say what, for after this verse it says (ibid. 9:7), "and Moses said to Aaron, approach the altar," and so on. Therefore they were compelled to say that this statement of Moses is that they should remove the evil inclination from their hearts.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:22: And his saying "that evil inclination" - the matter is that at the giving of the Torah, the filth of Israel's sins ceased, and they attained a level of prophecy, until they heard from the mouth of the Almighty, "I am" and "you shall have no other," and so on; and when they sinned with the calf, they returned to draw upon themselves the foreskin of the serpent and the evil inclination, so that they could not even look upon the face of an intermediary [angel], as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:18). And now, after the seven days of consecration, which were a partial repair for Aaron and all Israel through the repair of these offerings, Moses said to them: if you wish to see the glory of the LORD, which is the great gift they had before the [sin of the] calf, remove that evil inclination from your hearts. And by saying "that," he meant to say, that evil inclination which you drew upon yourselves - remove it from your hearts.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:23: And it has already been explained in chapter 4 that the heart has two chambers: one a dwelling for the good inclination, and one a dwelling for the evil inclination, which is the external one, a foreign god. And while a foreign god is in a person's heart, it is impossible for him to attain the glory of the LORD, which is unity - because the external one is a partition separating between him and the glory of the LORD. Rather, "remove the evil inclination from your hearts, and be all of you in one fear and one counsel to serve" - if you do so, "the glory of the LORD shall appear to you," what was hidden from you because of the partition of the inclination; for once you have removed the evil inclination from the heart, which is the second chamber of the heart, only one heart remains, which is the good inclination, and thereby the fear will be one, unified toward the Omnipresent, who is unique in the world. But while the evil inclination is in between, every act of service a person performs has in it a portion for the evil inclination, and the Omnipresent is not unified in it, since it is [now] a second [entity], and it has in it a portion for a "second," which is the foreskin of the evil inclination, a foreign god - and this is duality and idolatry. And therefore we were warned, "there shall be no foreign god within you," and they said (Shabbat 105b): what is the foreign god that is in a person's body? This is the evil inclination.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:24: And so too, "and you shall circumcise the foreskin of your hearts" (Deuteronomy 10:16) - and this verse is said in the passage (ibid. 10:12), "and now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you, but to fear" - and Scripture teaches us the matter of fear, how it should be: it says that it is through circumcising the foreskin of the heart, which is the evil inclination, which is a duality, a foreign god. And the reason: "for the LORD your God, He is God of gods," and so on - and just as He is One, so He wishes that we fear Him in unity, and that we not let the inclination partner in anything pertaining to His fear. And Israel, in the matter of the calf, blemished this by not protesting against the mixed multitude who made the calf, and flattered them - therefore He now warns that their service should be unified in one heart, with no ulterior motive whatsoever in the service of God; for any ulterior motive in service means that motive becomes the cause of the service, and it is a portion for a foreign god and is not unified for the sake of the Blessed Name. And just as one who worships idolatry and [also] worships the Blessed Name at all - his worship of the Blessed Name is not [true] worship at all, since in his worship of idolatry he denied the Holy One, blessed be He - so too, in his partnering the portion of the inclination, which is a foreign god, with divine worship, it has no portion in it at all, for the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes that His service be pure and clear, in one heart, without any admixture or refuse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:25: And this is the conclusion of the verse (ibid. 10:17), "who shows no favor and takes no bribe" - lest one say, since he performed a commandment, even though there is in it a portion for the evil inclination, the Holy One, blessed be He, will take His portion [and accept the rest] - to this it says, "shows no favor": one who has two faces to a commandment - a face toward people, so that they honor him, or he protects himself from mishaps of the inclination - and a face toward the commandment [itself] - the Holy One, blessed be He, does not accept it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:26: And likewise, "and takes no bribe" - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Rambam on Avot 4:22): what is a "bribe"? A bribe of commandments - meaning, one should not say, sin is thus and merits are thus, and the commandments performed will offset and cancel the sins against the merits, and he will remain without punishment; rather, for the sum of the sins he committed, since the evil inclination, who is a foreign god, who is the enemy, overpowered him, he will be punished regardless.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:27: And it is possible to say that this entire command is directed to the mixed multitude, who made the calf - for it first mentions (Leviticus 9:3), "and to the children of Israel," and afterward, "and Moses said, this thing" - and this "thing" was directed against the mixed multitude, who were the primary makers of the calf, and therefore it says, "remove that evil inclination from your hearts." And so it says, "and be in one fear and one counsel" - because they had nullified fear, it says that they should be in fear; and they had taken counsel together in several evil counsels to make the calf, as is explained in the Zohar - it says that they should be in one counsel, to serve. And if you do so, you will merit the glory of the LORD - and so it says (ibid. 9:24), "and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people," and it is already known that "the people" without qualification refers to the mixed multitude. And let it not trouble you that it says at the beginning of the passage, "Moses said to Israel" - for the mixed multitude were included within [the community of] Israel, and one is not precise about the term "children of Israel" as referring to the nation except in Scripture itself, not in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:28: Further, it is said that the author of this discourse was compelled to bring the verse (Deuteronomy 10:16), "and you shall circumcise the foreskin of your hearts," and so on, because he wished to explain that this verse, "this is the thing which the LORD commanded," refers to the removal of the inclination from the heart - and where do we find that He commanded this? To this he says, we find that He commanded this in the verse "and you shall circumcise," and so on. And he concludes the discourse: "if you do so, [the glory of the LORD] shall appear to you." It was difficult, [for one might ask]: the existence of removing the inclination is a [matter of] "you shall not do," and is not included in "you shall do" - for [Scripture] only warns of performing a commandment done with the hands, whereas circumcision of the heart is not [done] with the hands, but rather to remove evil beliefs and the like from one's heart, and it should not have mentioned the word "you shall do" at all. Rather, he says that the meaning of the verse is: "if you do so" - and he divided the verse with a sharp knife: "this is the thing which the LORD commanded" - namely, the removal of the inclination - "and if you shall do so" - to circumcise it and remove it - "then the glory of the LORD shall appear to you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:29: And by this [the verse means that] Israel and the mixed multitude all blemished with the calf, each according to his own category, and the blemish of idolatry blemishes the Shechinah, called "the glory of the LORD," as they explain in the Zohar (Tzav 27a) and in the Tikkunim (3b); and therefore this "thing," which is the Shechinah, you need to repair. And what is its repair? That you remove the evil inclination from your hearts - for when a person removes the evil inclination from his heart, so it is removed from the supernal heart [correspondingly].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:30: And because the repair of this attribute is through fear, since the essence of fear belongs to its side, it says, "and be all of you in one fear," and it explains the matter of fear - that just as He is unique in the world, so shall your service be unified before Him - meaning, just as He is unique in the world, being the Cause of all causes, the hidden One, wondrous and concealed, to whom the essence of fear is directed, as explained in chapter 1 of this Gate - so shall your service, which is the Shechinah, be unified without mixing any husk into it at all, as it is said (Psalms 19:10), "the fear of the LORD is pure" - that the Shechinah, called "fear," should be pure of all dross and all husks, of all extraneous thoughts, at the time of unification and service.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:31: And the reason is that the whole purpose of the unification we perform is to unify the Emanator and the emanated, that they all be one unity; and the Shechinah, who dwells with us, is to be raised so that she be unified above, through our prayer and our service. And if there is, in that prayer or in the commandment and the service, a portion for the [evil] inclination, then the external one is found grasping it, and it cannot ascend, and is not pure. And therefore it is explained in the Tikkunim (97b): and at the time a person needs to unify the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Shechinah, he must strip from himself all the thoughts that are husks, of which it is said (Proverbs 19:21), "many are the thoughts in a man's heart," and raise His Shechinah to Him in one single thought - this is "but the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:32: "And if you do so, the glory of the LORD shall appear to you" - meaning, if you do so, to purify the Shechinah from all the husks and unify her, "the glory of the LORD shall appear to you" - and see what we explained in chapter 2, in which sense it is called "the glory of the LORD." And we thus learn from this discourse that the essence of fear is that it be unified for the Blessed Name, and that nothing else be mixed into it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:33: And Rabbi Yehudah Ibn Farchi, peace be upon him, wrote concerning the reason for the commandment to fear, that the intent is that we should fear only the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, and not because of any angel or seraph - for Metatron, even though his name is like the name of his Master, is not to be feared; and this is (Deuteronomy 6:13), "the LORD your God shall you fear" - alone; and the reason is that no creature has the power to do good or evil except through His hand, blessed be He, and He gives power to all the angels to act. And a person who fears an angel or anything else demonstrates that he believes it has power of its own, and does not draw it from Him, blessed be He - and this resembles one who believes there are two domains, and he thereby denies the [divine] Principle. This is the reason for the essence of the fear of Heaven, which indicates His unity, and so on - to this point, in brief.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:34: In the Tikkunim (77a) they explain concerning the matter of fear that it should be fear of the Shechinah, whether in judgment or in mercy; in these words: Rabbi Shimon arose and said, Elazar my son, one who fears the Holy One, blessed be He, so that his children be favored and his wealth increase in this world, and if he lacks this he does not fear Him - this one does not make the fear of the LORD his essential [motive]; but one who fears the Holy One, blessed be He, whether in good or in distress - behold, this one makes the fear of the LORD his essential [motive] - to this point. And this is close to the fear already explained, for since fear is bound up with judgment and with mercy, it is one unity - and this is "the LORD, He is God" - and if the two are not bound together as one, it is a separation and appears as two domains, for the Infinite rests only in complete unity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:35: Further, I found in the book Sefer HaRokeach, in the introduction to the book, matters pertaining to fear, which I have seen fit to copy here; in these words: "Be shrewd in fear. Turn from evil and do good. Honor your parents. Seek peace between one man and his fellow. Rebuke your fellow. Guide him gently toward Heaven. Merit him in all your words. Distance yourself from scoffers and the reckless. Cleave to those who fear the LORD. Break your spirit and your desire. Rend the lock of your heart. Weep over the multitude of your sins. Confess and abandon wickedness. Plead with your Creator over the multitude of your transgressions, that He forgive your iniquities according to His abundant mercy. Pray to Him to place His fear upon your face, to plant His love in your heart, to serve Him with joy. Seek mercy for yourself and for the members of your household, that not one of them come to transgression, nor to anything ugly and sinful, and that he not be greedy after his throat, and not occupy himself with vain futility - for the Creator has no desire in eating and drinking; what advantage is there in toiling for the worm and the maggot? If you sin a little, let it seem much in your eyes, and repent. If you perform Torah and good deeds, say, for this I was created. Recognize your Creator, who made you. Fear the LORD your Maker. Consider that His glory fills the whole world. Walk in humility and gravity. Do not associate with scoffers. Do not sit with those who speak idle words. Let the fear of your King be between your eyes. Set your heart, for He sees all your deeds - He who searches the heart and examines the innermost parts knows all your thoughts. Consider that He made you and sustains you; He made you His eternal servant - therefore place His fear upon your face. Guard yourself against sinning. Walk before Him and be wholehearted, and your heart will be found faithful before Him - for He has no desire in fools, men of scorn and empty men who follow their inclination and are sustained by the desire of their lust, who desire the vain, futile delight of the world; and among men of [evil] speech there is no fear - behold, when calamity comes upon them they will cry to God and He will not hear, because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the LORD. One who guides himself with humility and fear becomes wise through fear; then you will understand the fear of the LORD, and find the knowledge of God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:36: "'The LORD your God shall you fear' - to include Torah scholars. A servant of the king is like the king, and one who honors him is as one who greets the presence of glory itself. Therefore, while your spirit is still within its sheath, return in the fear of your Creator. Cast your deeds upon the LORD, and your thoughts will be established. The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, to turn away from the snares of death. Remove from yourself hastiness, and stubbornness, and pride, and laziness. Hold fast to humility and peace, and do not envy those who do wrong, but rather [envy those in] the fear of the LORD all the day; and let the security of your times be the strength of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge - the fear of the LORD is its treasure. And though a man hide himself in secret places, shall I not see him? says the LORD - for are not My eyes roaming through all the earth? And know that there is a test in beauty, or in strength, or in honor, or in jealousy, or in wisdom, or in wealth, or in poverty, or in the strength of the inclination toward transgression. And know that the commandment and fear extinguish the fire of the inclination, and the Torah is a spice to remove evil thought" - to this point, to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:37: And among the virtues of fear is that one who fears the LORD does not fear the mishaps of this world, as it is said (Genesis 9:2), "and the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth" - and they explained "upon every" to include the harmful spirits. And regarding people it is said (Numbers 14:9), "and the LORD is with us, fear them not"; and so King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 56:5), "I will not fear; what can flesh do to me?"; and it says (Isaiah 51:12), "who are you, that you should fear mortal man, who shall die, and the son of man, who shall be made as grass?" - and many similar verses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:38: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, and his colleagues were praised for this virtue, as it says in the Zohar, Parashat Ki Tazria (46a), in these words, in brief: "surely you are none other than those of the household of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who fear nothing." And the intent is that he should be able to rebuke concerning the Torah and not fear them, along the lines of what is said (Isaiah 50:7), "I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed" - meaning, in a matter that is the service of God, he should not fear and should not be ashamed, as it says (Avot 5:20), "be bold as a leopard to do the will of your Father in Heaven."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:39: But nevertheless a person must feel shame before people in worldly matters that do not pertain to divine service, and must fear Torah scholars, as it is said (Deuteronomy 6:13), "the LORD your God shall you fear" - to include Torah scholars. And so they said in tractate Shabbat, chapter 2 (Shabbat 23b): one who fears the Sages will himself become a Torah scholar, and even if he is not fit for this, his words will be heard as though he were a Torah scholar - to this point.
